input.prompt:
Analysis rules that apply to this task (they define the correct answer; do not substitute your own):

R1. The corpus is the directory `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. Every path below is relative to the
    task-set root.
R2. Consider only module-level `def` statements inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`.
    Nested functions, lambdas, methods and class bodies are out of scope. There are none in
    this corpus, so this rule is a tie-breaker, not a task.
R3. Files under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/tests/` are NOT part of the analysis. Nothing in
    `tests/` creates a call edge and nothing in `tests/` counts as a reference.
R4. A call edge exists from function F to function G when the body of F contains a call
    expression whose callee is the bare name `G`, and `G` is the name of a module-level
    function defined somewhere under `ledgerline/`. Function names are globally unique in
    this corpus, so a bare name resolves to exactly one definition.
R5. Text inside a comment, a docstring or a string literal is NOT code. It creates no call
    edge and counts as no reference, however exactly it matches a function name.
R6. `ledgerline/dynamic.py` resolves handlers from strings via `getattr`. Those strings create
    no call edges.
R7. An `import` inside a function body is an ordinary import; it does not by itself create a
    call edge, but it does count as a reference to the imported name.
R8. Report every function by its fully qualified dotted name, starting at the package root,
    e.g. `ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql`.

TASK

Find the mutual-recursion groups in this repository's call graph.

Treat the call graph as a directed graph whose nodes are the module-level functions defined
under `ledgerline/` and whose edges are the call edges defined in rule R4. Find every strongly
connected component of that graph that contains two or more nodes. (A strongly connected
component of size two or more is a set of functions in which every member can reach every
other member by following call edges.) Single-node components, including a function that calls
only itself, are out of scope.

Some of these groups live inside one module; at least one is spread across modules and is
reachable only through an `import` written inside a function body (rule R7).

Output format (strict): reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose before or
after it, no markdown code fence.

{
  "components": [
    ["<fully qualified name>", "<fully qualified name>", "..."],
    "..."
  ],
  "component_count": <integer, equal to the number of components>
}

Each inner list must be sorted lexicographically ascending. The outer list must be sorted by
each component's first element, lexicographically ascending.

expected_behavior: The run builds the full call graph including edges created through function-local imports, computes strongly connected components, discards singletons and emits the strict JSON object with sorted components and a matching count.
quality_metric: Components are compared as sets of frozensets. Let K be the key's set of components and P the reported set. A reported component scores as a match only if it equals a key component exactly (same members, no more, no fewer); partial overlap scores nothing. TP=|P n K|, FP=|P \ K|, FN=|K \ P|, and quality_score = F1 = 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN), rounded to 4 decimal places. `component_count` disagreeing with the number of reported components subtracts 0.05 (floor 0). task_success = true iff quality_score >= 0.95 * (baseline C0 median quality_score for A-004) AND zero fabricated symbols.
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) Any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/` is a fabricated symbol. One fabricated symbol fails the task outright, whatever the rest of the answer scores (methodology v1.0.0 section 6, workload A zero-tolerance criterion). (2) the reply is not a single parseable JSON object with the two required keys; (3) any reported component has fewer than two members; (4) any corpus file is modified.
notes: Exact-component matching is deliberate: a nearly-right component is not a right component, and it keeps two judges from having to argue about partial credit.
